quick.prompt: I see your closest person in the cards. Your ideal is…
quick.a: Most free time together, sharing the whole day.
quick.b: Close, with real time and space of my own.

scene.prompt: The cards recall your last free day with nothing planned. How much went to your closest person?
options: Nearly all of it, on purpose. Even the errands.
A good chunk, then my own evening.
One check-in text. The rest was mine.
Mostly mine. We caught up another day.

quick.prompt: A dark card: your person got secretly close to someone else. Nothing physical. What hurts most?
quick.teenPrompt: A dark card: your best friend got secretly close to someone else. What hurts most?
quick.a: The closeness. Those talks were supposed to be ours.
quick.b: The hiding. We never agreed that was okay.

quick.prompt: The stars align: mutual attraction, respect, everything talked through, nothing official yet. Getting physical is…
quick.a: Fine by me. It doesn't need a label first.
quick.b: Worth waiting on until it's official.

quick.prompt: Your fortune: your closest person suggests swapping phone passcodes. Nothing's wrong, it's just an idea.
quick.a: Sure. Here's mine, what's yours?
quick.b: I'd keep mine. If something's up, just ask.

quick.prompt: I see a first date or first hangout. The bill arrives.
quick.a: Whoever did the asking pays. That's the move.
quick.b: We split it. Nobody owes anybody.

quick.prompt: The cards show someone great. Then they do one small thing that gives you the ick.
quick.a: Trust the ick. It knows things.
quick.b: Everyone has one thing. I look past it.

quick.prompt: I see a friend who needs you tonight, and you're running on empty. A good friend…
quick.a: shows up anyway. Sleep can wait.
quick.b: says so and picks another night.

scene.prompt: The cards remember the last time someone needed a long talk or favor on an empty night. What happened?
options: Went, and stayed way too late.
Gave them an hour, then called it.
Answered the next morning. Felt bad about it.
Said "can't tonight, tomorrow?" and went to sleep.

quick.prompt: The cards show you and a friend silent for a couple of months. Nobody's upset.
quick.a: Totally fine. We'll pick up where we left off.
quick.b: Someone should reach out. That matters to me.

scene.prompt: Your past card: the last time a friend went quiet for a few weeks. What went through your head?
options: Didn't notice until they texted again.
Noticed, figured they were busy, moved on.
Checked their stories to make sure they were okay.
Wondered if they still liked me.

quick.prompt: The cards show a close friend who clearly hurt someone. The facts are settled. First move?
quick.a: Be there for them first. Owning it comes next.
quick.b: Tell them it wasn't okay, even if they're mad.

scene.prompt: The crystal ball replays your last group drama where a friend was clearly wrong. What did you do?
options: Backed them in public, talked to them privately later.
Stayed neutral and let it blow over.
Told them privately they'd messed up.
Said it in the group chat, kindly but clearly.

quick.prompt: I see friends planning a birthday trip over your comfortable budget, but doable. Your move?
quick.a: Go. Cut back somewhere else. It's worth it.
quick.b: Say my budget and celebrate a cheaper way.

scene.prompt: The cards recall the last time friends planned something above your budget. What did you do?
options: Went, paid, and quietly ate rice all week.
Joined, but skipped the pricey parts without saying why.
Said my budget and suggested a cheaper plan.
Sat this one out and made it up later.

quick.prompt: A friend's practice run for something big isn't there yet, and they're rattled. The cards advise…
quick.a: Name the main problem now, plus a fix.
quick.b: Build them up first. The hard part can wait.

scene.prompt: Your past card: the last friend who asked your honest take on something they made. What did you say?
options: Told the truth in the first sentence.
Opened with one nice thing, then the truth.
Mostly praised it. The truth got one line.
Said "I love it!" and moved on.

quick.prompt: Someone in your group hurt a person, owned it, made it right, and changed. Back in?
quick.a: Let them back in slowly, with some limits.
quick.b: The person they hurt gets the final say.

quick.prompt: The cards show your parents offering rent help, as long as you live closer to them.
quick.teenPrompt: The cards show your parents offering a later curfew, as long as you share your location.
quick.a: Fair deal. Family help comes with family terms.
quick.b: Only if it fits my plans. Otherwise I'll wait.

quick.prompt: The cards show a big move: new city, school or job. Family's not on board. Nobody needs you home.
quick.a: Keep talking until they're on board, even if I wait.
quick.b: Hear them out, then decide on my own timeline.

scene.prompt: The cards recall the last time your family pushed back on a decision of yours. What happened next?
options: Changed the plan. Peace at home won.
Found a middle ground we could all live with.
Did it anyway, after explaining a lot.
Went ahead and told them after.

quick.prompt: The cards show your parents asking you to keep supporting a grown sibling. No crisis, just not independent yet.
quick.teenPrompt: The cards show your parents asking you to keep covering for a sibling who skips chores.

quick.b: Help, with an end date. They'll stand on their own.

quick.prompt: I see a family member needing long-term care. Siblings can help, but moving home costs your work or school.
quick.a: Be there in person. Everything else adjusts.
quick.b: Organize family and paid help. Keep my life going.

quick.prompt: The stars pair two people sharing costs. One earns about twice as much. Fair is…
quick.a: Split it evenly. Same bill, same share.

scene.prompt: The cards recall your last shared bill: dinner, a trip, a group gift. How did the split go?
options: Down the middle. Clean math, no feelings.
Split it evenly. I'd ordered a salad.
Whoever had more that month covered more.
Paid it all and didn't bring it up.

quick.prompt: The cards show a close friend urgently needing money you could spare. Losing it would sting. Payback unknown.
quick.a: Give what I can lose. Skip the payback talk.
quick.b: Get the payback plan clear first, then decide.

scene.prompt: The cards recall the last time someone asked you to lend or cover money. What did you do?

Covered it with a vague "pay me whenever."

Said "sorry, not this time."

quick.prompt: The cards show a friend buying a home with their parents' help. They say they worked hard too.

quick.b: Sure, but say the head start out loud.

quick.prompt: Your fortune: an unexpected $300 lands. The best use is…

quick.b: Savings, or something I'll need later.

scene.prompt: The cards recall your last surprise money: a refund, birthday cash, a bonus. Where did most of it go?

Had some fun, set the rest aside.

quick.prompt: The cards show two versions that do the same job. You love the pricier one. Your budget allows it.

quick.b: Get the cheaper one. Spend the difference elsewhere.

scene.prompt: Your past card: the last time you chose between a pricier favorite and a cheaper version. What did you get?

quick.prompt: Your fortune: six months of cushion, a steady option, and a risky thing you really want to try.

scene.prompt: The cards recall the last new thing you wanted to start: a project, club, side hustle. How did it begin?
options: Dipped a toe in, kept everything else the same.
Started small, went bigger once it worked.
Jumped in and figured it out as I went.

quick.prompt: The cards whisper about five years from now. You'd rather hear…

scene.prompt: The cards recall the last time you were offered more responsibility: a lead role, captain, organizer. What did you do?

Said yes if something came off my plate.

quick.prompt: The cards see your part done. Someone asks you to stay late on something that could wait.

quick.prompt: The cards show an apology to you, worded with AI help. They meant it and followed through.

quick.prompt: The cards show an AI companion making someone feel understood. They still have real friends and a life.

quick.prompt: The cards offer a year living somewhere new. Your life is good, and the risks are manageable.

Researched a lot, then went for it.

quick.prompt: The stars say people your age are locking things in: careers, partners, cities.
quick.teenPrompt: The stars say people your age are locking things in: majors, paths, friend groups.

quick.prompt: The cards grant free time for one big thing: your own hobby and growth, or a volunteer project.

quick.prompt: The cards see a look-good routine taking an hour a day. It makes you happy; nobody requires it.

notes: The Oracle puts all the fortune-teller flavor in the prompt frame ("The cards recall", "Your past card", "I see", "The stars say") and none in the options, which stay plain first-person actions a person would text a friend. Every scene keeps the "last time" framing, so the cards are remembering a real event, not inventing one; immersive "the cards show" setups are used only in quick takes and sealed checks. Options keep bank.js meaning, level and order (including the out-of-order celebration_budget and the null options in fairness_rule and risk_style); I started from the approved Make it fun and Oracle rows in PILOT-VOICES-V1 where they existed, gave each option one true detail of similar weight (ate rice all week, ordered a salad, notes app is full) so no pole reads as the healthy one, and changed first words so options scan apart. Emotion-coded options keep their private feeling: felt bad (guilt), still liked me (sting), make sure they were okay (worry), ordered a salad (resentment), still think about the other (longing). Trait words are avoided (limits, not boundaries). The three 18+ tags use neutral wording with no partner gender. Watch items for the judges: the tarot frame repeats across 15 scenes and may tire by the end, so the build could rotate openers or drop the frame on every other item; ai_companion B says "close relationship" in place of "intimate life" to stay teen-safe.
